_meta.indication: REVCOVI is indicated for the treatment of adenosine deaminase severe combined immune deficiency (ADA-SCID) in pediatric and adult patients.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, multicenter, single-arm, one-way crossover study of patients receiving Adagen therapy who were converted to REVCOVI.
pivotal_trials.population: 6 patients with ADA-SCID, 8 to 37 years of age, receiving therapy with Adagen.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: metabolic detoxification defined as a trough dAXP concentration ≤ 0.02 mmol/L and maintenance of detoxification during the treatment phase; key secondary endpoint: adequate trough ADA activity ≥ 15 mmol/hr/L.
pivotal_trials.result: Five of six patients reached the 21-week endpoint; these patients had trough plasma ADA activity ≥ 15 mmol/hr/L at 88/89 timepoints and maintained detoxification. Mean trough plasma ADA activity on REVCOVI at 0.2 mg/kg/week was 34.3 ± 6.6 mmol/hr/L versus 14.2 ± 5.1 mmol/hr/L on Adagen at 30 U/kg/week.

pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm clinical study with an Evaluation phase (5-week Dose Adjustment Period and 16-week Dose Maintenance Period) and a Continuous Administration (Extension) Phase.
pivotal_trials.population: 4 patients with ADA-SCID: two males (age 25 years and 3.4 months) and two females (age 16 years and 4.3 months).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Detoxification (trough dAXP ≤ 0.02 mmol/L) and adequate trough ADA activity (≥ 15 mmol/hr/L).
pivotal_trials.result: All four patients achieved and maintained detoxification (trough dAXP ≤ 0.02 mmol/L) throughout the 21-week Treatment Phase; serum ADA activity increased for all four, with three achieving activity over 15 mmol/hr/L during the Dose Maintenance Period.

key_safety: The most common adverse reactions were cough (50%) and vomiting (33%). Warnings include increased risk of injection site bleeding in patients with thrombocytopenia and delay in improvement of immune function.
target_moa: Elapegademase-lvlr provides an exogenous source of ADA enzyme, which catalyzes deamination of adenosine/deoxyadenosine; in ADA deficiency elevated adenosine causes T-lymphopenia, so replacement decreases toxic adenosine/deoxyadenosine nucleotides and increases lymphocyte number.
modality: Enzyme (PEGylated recombinant adenosine deaminase enzyme replacement therapy).

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an advisory committee, as it is not the first ADA enzyme replacement therapy for ADA-SCID and did not raise significant safety or efficacy concerns.

On June 7, 2017, Fast Track development program designation was granted for the investigation of EZN-2279 for the treatment of adenosine deaminase severe combined immunodeficiency (ADA SCID).
On December 15, 2017, a request for Breakthrough Therapy Designation (BTD) for the treatment of ADA, submitted on November 3, 2017 was denied (See letter dated November 3, 2017 in DARRTS).

On July 27, 2018, a letter was issued to the Applicant, notifying that the review classification is changed to from Standard to Priority; however, the regulatory decision goal date would not be changed, meaning the PDUFA goal date would remain 08/24/2018.
We also inform you that you have been granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher, as provided under section 529 of the FDCA.

requirement.text: 3497-1: Conduct a study enrolling ADA-SCID naive patients started on de novo ERT with REVCOVI or converted from Adagen to REVCOVI, over 2 years, following patients until the last enrolled patient has 2 years of follow up.

citations.quote: 3497-1 To conduct a study to enroll ADA-SCID naïve patients started on de novo enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) with REVCOVI or converted from Adagen to REVCOVI including patient transitioned from the Study STP-2279-002, over the course of 2 years and continue to follow those patients until the last enrolled patient has 2 years of follow up. Patients who are expected to receive 3 to 4 months of ERT prior to proceeding to hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) or gene therapy will be included and contribute data to the analyses.
